files.lesson.md: --- order: 6 unit: models10 node: AC9M10A04 n2 uses: [AC9M10A03 n1, AC9M10A03 n3] # a constant ratio; y = a(bˣ) read from a graph assumes: [AC9M10A03 n4] # same base both sides, for the doubling time in Make connection: compound-savings title: Writing the model summary: "A rate of r% a year multiplies by 1 + r/100 each year. Write A = a(bⁿ) with the starting amount a and the growth or decay factor b, then use it to answer a question in dollars." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A savings account says '5% interest a year'. What does 5% a year really do to $1,000?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8387 url: http://127.0.0.1:8387/index.html readySelector: "#sl-r" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: savings.yml#explain-pic, caption: "Both start at $1,000 and gain $50 in the first year. The solid curve earns 5% on the new balance each year; the dashed line adds the same $50 every year." } explainClip: query: { code: "@savings.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "A rate each year multiplies, not adds" say: "A rate each year multiplies, not adds." clip: - caption: { text: "The dashed line adds the same dollars every year.", say: "The dashed line adds the same dollars every year." } - wait: 600 - click: Make r bigger - wait: 600 - caption: { text: "The solid curve earns on what it has already earned.", say: "The solid curve earns on what it has already earned." } - wait: 600 - caption: { text: "A higher rate pulls the curve away faster.", say: "A higher rate pulls the curve away faster." } - wait: 1200 --- You put $1,000 in a savings account. The account adds interest once a year, and the next year's interest is worked out on the new balance. The rate is made up for this lesson: real rates change, and accounts have fees and tax. ## Predict: after two years ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to the balance after two years shows who adds $50 twice (1,100) and who sees that the second year's 5% is worked out on 1,050." check: type: predict q: "After 1 year, $1,000 at 5% a year is worth $1,050. How much is it worth after 2 years?" options: - "$1{,}100$" - "$1{,}102.50$" - "$1{,}050$" - "$1{,}125$" actual: "$1,102.50. The second year's interest is 5% of 1,050, which is 52.50, not 50. So the balance is 1,050 × 1.05 = 1,102.50. Adding 50 twice would give 1,100." ``` The bars show the balance for the first year. Make a guess before you check. ## Run: a rate each year ```step stage: run insight: "A rate of r% a year multiplies the balance by 1 + r/100 each year, so it earns on what it has already earned. The dashed line earns the same dollars every year." try: { playground: board, starter: "savings.yml#run", height: 640 } check: { type: board, text: "Set $r$ to 5, so the account pays 5% a year. Read the table after 2 years and after 10 years. Does the 2-year value match your prediction?", when: "r = 5" } ``` The solid curve multiplies the balance by $1 + r/100$ each year. The dashed line adds the same dollars every year. The chart runs out of room, so read the big numbers from the table. ## Investigate: the growth factor ```step stage: investigate insight: "5% a year is a factor of 1.05, not 0.05: the old balance stays, and 5% of it is added. A decay of 8% a year is a factor of 0.92. Maya multiplies by the rate alone." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "An account grows by $6\\%$ a year. What do you multiply the balance by each year?" answer: "1.06" feedback: - ["0.06", "0.06 is 6% on its own. You keep the whole balance and add 6% of it: 1 + 0.06."] - ["6", "6 would multiply the balance by 6. 6% is 0.06 of the balance."] explain: "The whole balance stays (1) and 6% of it is added (0.06): 1.06." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#maya" text: "Maya writes the model for $1,000 at 5% a year. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: growth-factor-is-rate explain: "Line 2: multiplying by 0.05 keeps only 5% of the balance. To grow by 5% you keep all of it and add 5% more: multiply by 1.05." - check: type: question q: "A car loses $8\\%$ of its value each year. What do you multiply its value by each year?" options: ["0.92", "0.08", "1.08", "8"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "0.08 keeps only 8% of the value. A car keeps 92%.", "1.08 would make the value grow by 8%.", "8 multiplies the value by 8."] explain: "It keeps 100% − 8% = 92% of its value: 0.92." ``` ### Rate to factor Here's how to write the model from the words. ```worked \$2000 \text{ at } 3\% \text{ a year} :: Write the balance after n years. a = 2000 :: The starting amount. b = 1 + 0.03 = 1.03 :: Keep the balance and add 3% of it. A = 2000(1.03^n) :: Starting amount times the factor, n times. A = 2000(1.03^5) :: After 5 years. A = 2318.55 :: Rounded to the cent. Always put the unit: dollars. ``` Now try one on paper: $500$ at $4\%$ a year. Find the balance after 2 years, in dollars. ### Find the mistake Read Maya's working. What does 5% a year do to the balance? ### A falling value Think about what is kept. ## Modify: change the rate ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a longer wait, a falling value and a rate of 0." try: { playground: board, starter: "savings.yml#vary", height: 640 } tasks: - hint: ["Set $r$ to 7. Look down the table for the first value over 2,000.", "Year 10 gives 1,967; try year 11."] check: { type: answer, q: "Set $r$ to 7. In which year does the balance first pass $2,000$? (The table has some years; work out the ones in between.)", answer: "11", feedback: [["10", "At year 10 the balance is 1,967, just under 2,000. Try the next year."], ["20", "20 is the end of the table, not the first year over 2,000. Look at years 9 to 12."]], explain: "1,000 × 1.07¹⁰ = 1,967 and 1,000 × 1.07¹¹ = 2,105, so year 11 is the first." } - hint: ["The factor for losing 15% is 0.85.", "$20000 \\times 0.85 \\times 0.85$."] check: { type: answer, q: "A car worth $20,000$ loses 15% of its value each year. What is it worth after 2 years, in dollars?", answer: "14450", feedback: [["14000", "That takes off 15% of 20,000 twice. Each year takes 15% of the new value: multiply by 0.85 twice."], ["17000", "That's the value after 1 year. Multiply by 0.85 again."]], explain: "20,000 × 0.85 = 17,000 and 17,000 × 0.85 = 14,450." } - hint: "Set $r$ to 0 and look at the table." check: type: question q: "Edge case: set $r$ to 0. The account pays 0% a year. What is the growth factor, and what happens to the balance?" options: ["The factor is 1 and the balance stays at $1,000", "The factor is 0 and the balance is $0", "The factor is 0 and the balance stays at $1,000"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A factor of 0 would wipe out the balance. 0% adds nothing: 1 + 0 = 1.", "The factor is 1 + 0 = 1, not 0."] explain: "1 + 0/100 = 1, and multiplying by 1 changes nothing." ``` ### Waiting for 2,000 ### A car ### A rate of 0 ## Practise: write the model ```step stage: practise insight: "Turning a rate into a factor, writing and using A = a(bⁿ), and (review) solving with the same base." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "An account grows by $9\\%$ a year. What is the growth factor?" answer: "1.09" feedback: - ["0.09", "0.09 is 9% on its own. Keep the whole balance and add 9%: 1 + 0.09."] explain: "1 + 0.09 = 1.09." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "Just the decimal: what is $9\\%$ as a decimal?", answer: 0.09, explain: "9% = 9 ÷ 100 = 0.09. Now add it to 1." } - check: type: answer q: "$200$ is invested at $10\\%$ a year. What is the balance after 2 years, in dollars?" answer: "242" feedback: - ["240", "That adds 10% of 200 twice. The second year's 10% is of the new balance: 200 × 1.1 × 1.1."] explain: "200 × 1.1 = 220 and 220 × 1.1 = 242." - check: type: answer q: "A model is $A = 3000(1.02^n)$. What is the starting amount, in dollars?" answer: "3000" feedback: - ["1.02", "1.02 is the growth factor. The starting amount is the number in front, where n = 0."] explain: "At n = 0 the power is 1, so A = 3000." - check: type: number q: "Review: solve $3^x = 81$. What is $x$?" answer: 4 explain: "81 = 3⁴, so x = 4." ``` ### The growth factor ### Two years ### The starting amount ### Review From the last unit: solving with the same base. ## Make: back to the savings ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the savings: the compounding balance beats the same dollars added each year, and the gap grows." tasks: - hint: ["Simple interest adds $50 each year for 10 years.", "Compound: $1000 \\times 1.05^{10}$."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "$1,000$ at 5% a year for 10 years. The dashed line adds $50 every year. By how many dollars does the compounding balance beat it? Round to the cent." steps: - ["$1000 \\times 1.05^{10} = 1628.89$", "the compounding balance"] - ["$1000 + 50 \\times 10 = 1500$", "the same dollars each year"] - ["$1628.89 - 1500 = 128.89$", "how much more"] answer: "128.89" answerLabel: "Dollars more" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["1628.89", "That's the compounding balance. Subtract the 1,500."] - ["500", "That's the 50 a year added up: 1,500 − 1,000. Compare the two final balances."] criteria: - "I worked out both balances." - "I used 1.05, not 0.05, as the factor." - "I subtracted in the right order and gave dollars." explain: "1,628.89 − 1,500 = 128.89. The extra comes from earning interest on interest." - check: type: question q: "A friend says: 'The model A = 1000(1.05ⁿ) says my money grows forever.' What would you say?" options: ["It's a model with made-up rates: real rates change, and there are fees and tax", "It's exactly right: rates never change", "It's wrong because the balance can't grow", "It's wrong because n must be 0"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Rates change, and accounts have fees and tax. The model assumes one fixed rate.", "The balance does grow in the model.", "n is the number of years and can be any number of years."] explain: "The model holds one rate for every year. Real accounts change the rate and may charge fees and tax." ``` ### Compound against simple Back to the savings. Work this out on paper first, then type your answer. ### How much to trust it The rate and the $1,000$ are made up. The shape is the point: a rate each year multiplies, so the last years add the most. Sources: the $1,000$ and the 5% a year are made up for this lesson and are not an offer. Your class can check real figures with a savings calculator, such as [MoneySmart's compound interest calculator](https://moneysmart.gov.au/saving/compound-interest-calculator) (ASIC); it also shows the effect of fees and tax. **Also used in** - **Money.** Loans grow the same way when interest is added to what is owed. - **Science.** A population growing 3% a year, or a drug leaving the body at 12% an hour, uses the same model. - **Next lesson.** Two models at once: when does one overtake the other? ```teacher summary: Students turn a rate a year into a growth or decay factor, write A = a(bⁿ), and use it to answer a question in dollars (AC9M10A04, node 2). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can turn a percentage rate into a growth or decay factor. - I can write a model with a starting amount and a factor. - I can use the model to find a value and say what it means in dollars. struggle: "Using the rate on its own as the factor (0.05 for 5% growth). Say 'what stays, and what is added?': 100% stays, plus 5%." before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need the ratio idea from lesson 1 and y = a(bˣ) from lesson 3. The one idea: a rate a year is a factor, 1 + r for growth and 1 − r for decay. The model then reads A = a(bⁿ): a is the starting amount, b the factor, n the number of years. The rates and the $1,000 are made up and are not an offer. Real accounts change the rate and may charge fees and tax; the model assumes one fixed rate. The sources line points at ASIC's MoneySmart calculator for real figures: check the page before class. Rounding: keep the exact power in the calculator and round to the cent at the end. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose 1,100 added $50 twice. Don't correct it yet." - "Run: ask students to compare the two curves after 10 and 20 years, and say what the dashed line is leaving out." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the compound against simple task in Make are worked on paper first. Look for 1.04, not 0.04, in the working." - "Modify: before the rate of 0, ask what 1 + 0 is." stuck: - see: A student uses 0.05 as the factor (Maya's mistake). ask: If you multiply 1,000 by 0.05, do you have more or less than before? fix: "A bigger balance means a factor above 1. Write 1 + 0.05 and say what each part is: the balance you keep and the interest you add." - see: A student works 2 years as 1,000 + 50 + 50. ask: Is the second year's 5% of 1,000 or of the new balance? fix: Work year 2 as 1,050 × 1.05. Interest is paid on the interest. - see: A student writes the decay factor as 0.08 for losing 8%. ask: What share of the value is kept? fix: "It keeps 92%: 0.92. Factor = 1 − rate for a decay." stretch: "How long to double at 7% a year? Try the table, then write 1.07ⁿ = 2 and see why the same-base trick doesn't work for it. Rule of 72: 72 ÷ 7 is about 10. How close is that?" support: "A table with an extra row: 'what stays' and 'what is added'. Fill it for 5%, 10% and 20% before writing the factor." leads: > Next: two models at once, such as a steady saver and a compounding one, and finding where they meet. Where it leads in class: loans, depreciation and population models. exit: q: A phone loses 20% of its value each year and costs 900 new. Write the model and find its value after 3 years. a: "A = 900(0.8ⁿ). After 3 years: 900 × 0.8³ = 460.80 dollars." explain: > A rate a year changes the balance by the same **share** each year, so the model multiplies. - Growth of r%: factor $b = 1 + r/100$, for example 5% is 1.05. - Decay of r%: factor $b = 1 - r/100$, for example 8% is 0.92. The model is $A = a(b^n)$: $a$ is the starting amount and $n$ is the number of years. Always give the answer in dollars (or the unit in the question). sources: - title: "MoneySmart compound interest calculator (ASIC): a real calculator to check the model's figures, with fees and tax" url: https://moneysmart.gov.au/saving/compound-interest-calculator checked: 2026-10-25 - title: "Made up for this lesson: the $1,000 and the 5% a year are not an offer from a bank." url: https://tutorials.learningwaypoints.com/maths/functions/writing-the-model/ checked: 2026-10-25 ```

# Boards for "Writing the model". x is the number of years, r is the yearly rate in per cent (made up, not an offer
# from a bank). The balance starts at $1,000 and is A = 1000(1 + r/100)^x. The dashed line adds the same dollars
# each year (simple interest at the same rate) so the two can be compared.

# region: run
widget: graph
x: 0, 20
y: 0, 3000
grid: 5, 500
axes: Time (years), Balance ($)
slider r: 0, 10, 3, 1
plot: y = 1000((1 + r/100)^x)
plot: y = 1000 + 10rx, dashed
table: 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 20
# endregion

# region: explain
widget: graph
x: 0, 20
y: 0, 3000
grid: 5, 500
axes: Time (years), Balance ($)
slider r: 0, 10, 5, 1
plot: y = 1000((1 + r/100)^x)
plot: y = 1000 + 10rx, dashed
table: 0, 1, 2, 5, 10
# endregion

# region: explain-pic
widget: graph
x: 0, 20
y: 0, 3000
grid: 5, 500
axes: Time (years), Balance ($)
plot: y = 1000(1.05^x)
plot: y = 1000 + 50x, dashed
table: 0, 1, 2, 5, 10
# endregion

# region: vary
widget: graph
x: 0, 20
y: 0, 3000
grid: 5, 500
axes: Time (years), Balance ($)
slider r: 0, 10, 7, 1
plot: y = 1000((1 + r/100)^x)
plot: y = 1000 + 10rx, dashed
table: 0, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 20
# endregion
files.working.txt:
# Maya's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: maya
An account pays 5% a year. I start with $1,000. What is the model?
5% is 0.05, so each year the balance is multiplied by 0.05.
So A = 1000 x 0.05^n, where n is the number of years.
After 1 year that gives 1000 x 0.05 = 50.
Fifty dollars is less than I started with, but that can't be right. Maybe I rounded.
# endregion
